question: Cyclosporine, tacrolimus, and sirolimus are classified as immunosuppressants. Which of the following correctly describes their primary mechanism?

answers.text: Cyclosporine and tacrolimus inhibit calcineurin; sirolimus inhibits mTOR

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Cyclosporine (CsA) and tacrolimus (FK506) bind their respective immunophilins (cyclophilin and FKBP12) and inhibit calcineurin, preventing IL-2 transcription. Sirolimus also binds FKBP12 but inhibits mTOR instead.

answers.text: All three inhibit calcineurin via different immunophilin complexes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Sirolimus forms the FKBP12 complex but targets mTOR, not calcineurin. Only cyclosporine and tacrolimus are calcineurin inhibitors.

answers.text: Cyclosporine inhibits mTOR; tacrolimus and sirolimus inhibit calcineurin

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. It is cyclosporine and tacrolimus that inhibit calcineurin. Sirolimus is the mTOR inhibitor.

answers.text: All three prevent allograft rejection by directly depleting circulating T-lymphocytes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. These agents do not deplete T-cells; they block T-cell activation signalling pathways (calcineurin or mTOR).

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Classification block. The key distinction is that cyclosporine and tacrolimus both inhibit calcineurin (via different immunophilins), whereas sirolimus inhibits mTOR.
Well done! Understanding the mechanistic distinction between calcineurin inhibitors and mTOR inhibitors is essential for choosing between these agents and predicting their toxicity profiles.
